reports.text: Specimen: skeletal muscle, left vastus lateralis, open biopsy (fresh and fixed portions). Frozen and paraffin sections show perifascicular atrophy, with small, basophilic fibers concentrated at the edges of fascicles. Perivascular inflammatory infiltrates in the perimysium, predominantly lymphocytes. Scattered necrotic and regenerating fibers. No rimmed vacuoles, no inclusions. Special stains and enzyme histochemistry otherwise unremarkable for this pattern.
reports.conclusion: Inflammatory myopathy with perifascicular atrophy and perivascular inflammation, consistent with dermatomyositis.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY FOLLOW-UP - 01/21/2026

She returns to go over the workup for the problem first evaluated by dermatology in July 2024. Over the last six months she has had more trouble with stairs and with lifting her arms; brushing her hair now tires her out, and she notices her neck feels weak holding her head up while sitting. No dysphagia or dyspnea. No regular medications. NKDA.

PSH: cholecystectomy 2014, tubal ligation 1999.
FH: mother - autoimmune thyroiditis; maternal aunt - rheumatoid arthritis; father - hypertension.
SH: high school math teacher; never smoked; wine 1-2 glasses a week.

Exam: Symmetric proximal weakness in arms and legs; neck flexors 4/5. Violaceous rash of the eyelids. Scaly red patches over the knuckles. Lungs clear.

Results:
- CK 3,480 U/L today (3,120 in November). AST 104, ALT 78.
- Myositis panel: anti-Mi-2 positive; remaining myositis-specific antibodies negative.
- EMG 12/10: irritable myopathy, proximal.
- Muscle biopsy (L vastus lateralis) 01/06: perifascicular atrophy with perivascular inflammation - consistent with dermatomyositis.
- Pre-treatment screening: HBsAg nonreactive, HCV Ab nonreactive, QuantiFERON negative.

Assessment: Dermatomyositis, confirmed by antibody, electrodiagnostic and biopsy findings.

Plan:
1. Prednisone 60 mg each morning. Will taper by response.
2. Methotrexate 15 mg once weekly, folic acid 1 mg daily. No alcohol beyond an occasional glass. CBC and liver tests every 4-6 weeks at first.
3. Vitamin D3 1000 units daily; calcium through diet.
4. CT chest, abdomen and pelvis for age-appropriate malignancy screening in adult dermatomyositis; her mammogram, Pap and colonoscopy are current.
5. Please consider bone density and pneumococcal vaccination with her PCP.
6. Return in 8 weeks.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Update from rheumatology
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi - rheumatology confirmed the dermatomyositis. I started prednisone 60 mg yesterday and the methotrexate this Sunday, plus folic acid and vitamin D. They said you might want to do a bone scan and a pneumonia vaccine. CT scan is booked for Feb 4. Should I come in?

documents.title: RE: Update from rheumatology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update, glad you have a plan. Yes - let's see you after the CT. The front desk will offer Feb 11. We'll give the pneumonia vaccine then and order the bone density test. Prednisone can raise blood sugar, so we'll check it at the visit.

reports.text: CT of the chest with IV contrast, performed with the abdomen and pelvis. Lungs are clear without nodules, consolidation, ground-glass or reticular opacity. No interstitial lung disease. Airways patent. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Heart size normal. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymphadenopathy. Thyroid and visualized breast tissue unremarkable. No osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Normal CT chest. No mass, adenopathy or interstitial lung disease.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys normal in appearance. Gallbladder surgically absent; no biliary dilatation. Bowel normal in caliber without wall thickening or mass. Uterus and adnexa unremarkable for age. No ascites. No retroperitoneal, mesenteric or pelvic lymphadenopathy. Bones without suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of malignancy in the abdomen or pelvis. Post-cholecystectomy.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to catch up after rheumatology. Dermatomyositis now confirmed (anti-Mi-2 positive, myopathic EMG, biopsy with perifascicular atrophy). Three weeks into prednisone 60 mg daily; methotrexate 15 mg weekly with folic acid and vitamin D3 1000 units.

Says the stairs feel a bit easier already. Took methotrexate the last 3 Sundays without nausea. CT last week normal - she had read the report and was relieved.

Exam: BP 126/80. Weight up about 1.5 kg. Lids still dusky. Strength in the hip flexors 4/5, shoulders 4+/5. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Dermatomyositis - treatment per rheumatology. Reviewed weekly (not daily) methotrexate dosing; she has a pill box marked for Sundays.
2. Glucocorticoid therapy - BMP for glucose today. DXA ordered. Vitamin D on board, dietary calcium ok (yogurt, milk).
3. Immunosuppressed - PCV20 given today. Flu and COVID already this season. Shingrix complete (2023). No live vaccines.
4. Follow up in summer, or sooner.

reports.text: Dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry of the lumbar spine (L1-L4) and left hip. All vertebral levels evaluable. Lumbar spine T-score -0.9. Total hip T-score -0.4. Indication: long-term glucocorticoid therapy.

documents.body: Good news - your bone density is normal (spine -0.9, hip -0.4). Keep up the vitamin D and calcium from food. We'll repeat it in a couple of years if you're still on prednisone. Your sugar on the 11th was fine too.

Summer check-in. Dermatomyositis much improved - she finished the school year without trouble on the stairs and is gardening again. On prednisone 20 mg daily since mid-May, methotrexate 15 mg Sundays, folic acid, D3. No mouth sores, no cough, no breathlessness. A few pounds up on prednisone.

Exam: BP 128/80. Wt 71.5 kg. Lids nearly clear, knuckles faint pink. Strength 5-/5 hip flexors, otherwise 5/5. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
1. Dermatomyositis, responding. CK, CMP, CBC today (also covers rheum's monitoring labs this cycle - will forward).
2. Prednisone effects - A1c today. BP fine. DXA normal in Feb.
3. Health maintenance: flu and COVID in the fall (inactivated only). Mammogram due November.
4. Rheumatology next in August.
